clue.text: More than one place beside river

indicators.note: beside says the two pieces sit next to each other, the place first

parts.note: PL is the standard abbreviation for place, as in street names
the Ural is a river flowing from Russia into the Caspian Sea

explanation.surface: A grammar note about a spot lying next to a river, perhaps one of several.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a word form denoting more than a single thing is the plural form.

clue.text: Medicine from America at bottom of crate initially covered by fibrous substance

indicators.note: in a down clue, at bottom of places the American letters below the rest
covered by means wrapped inside, so the crate letter goes inside the lint

parts.note: lint is a soft fibrous material used to dress wounds

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word crate

parts.note: US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: A shipment of medicine from the States found under packing material at the bottom of a crate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes C from 'crate'; 'covered by' puts it inside LINT; 'at bottom of' puts US under that in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A linctus is a syrupy cough medicine.

clue.text: Remarkable king on time turning up

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading the word from the bottom upward, so backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A monarch who is punctual, which is quite unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reads ERA upwards in this down entry, giving ARE beneath R; 'on' puts the king on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means unusual, seldom found, hence remarkable.

clue.text: Card game with stake involving hard ambiguity

parts.note: loo is an old gambling card game

indicators.note: involving means including, so the stake wraps round the hard letter

parts.note: a pole is a stake, a post driven into the ground
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A gambler's card game played for high stakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts H inside POLE. 'stake' suggests betting, but it is a post.
explanation.definitionFit: A loophole is a gap or ambiguity in rules that lets someone evade them.

clue.text: Criticism when leader's

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Criticism when leader's (6)', is cut short: CENSURE less its leader gives the letters, but the words after 'leader's' (its indicator, e.g. 'gone', and the definition) are missing, and no search found the full clue.

clue.text: Fake tears, appearing distressed on conclusion of quiz

indicators.note: distressed means agitated or damaged, so the letters of tears are jumbled
conclusion of picks the last letter of the word quiz

explanation.surface: Crocodile tears from a contestant upset at the end of a quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' rearranges TEARS into ERSAT; 'on conclusion of' takes Z from 'quiz' to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz means artificial, an inferior imitation or substitute.

clue.text: One cheers up, entering bid, making addition

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the reversed pair goes into the bid word

parts.note: to bid someone come is to summon them

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the pair is backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: An auction bidder cheering as their offer goes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns I and TA into ATI; 'entering' puts that inside SUMMON. 'cheers' means thanks here, not a shout.
explanation.definitionFit: Summation means the act of adding up, totalling.

clue.text: Note colour on very big screen

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
red is a colour
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, very big

explanation.surface: A colour note pinned onto a huge display screen.
explanation.walkthrough: A reredos is the ornamental screen behind a church altar.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is a decorated partition behind an altar, a type of church screen.

clue.text: Poor writer angry to be robbed of folio

parts.note: a pen is the tool a writer writes with, standing for the writer

indicators.note: being robbed of something means losing it, so a letter is taken out of the angry word

parts.note: furious means very angry
F is the abbreviation for folio, a page or book size

explanation.surface: A hard-up author furious at having a manuscript page stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be robbed of' removes F (folio) from FURIOUS, leaving URIOUS after PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Penurious describes someone living in extreme poverty, utterly destitute.

clue.text: Exercises before sessions incorporating quantity of work on composer's last opera

indicators.note: before says the exercises come ahead of the rest

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercises

indicators.note: incorporating means taking inside, so the sessions word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: times can mean sessions or occasions
an erg is a unit of work in physics

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word composer's

explanation.surface: A singer's warm-ups and practice sessions before rehearsing a composer's final opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorporating' puts ERG and R ('composer's last') inside TIMES; PE goes before. Peter Grimes is Britten's opera, though not his last.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Grimes is a 1945 opera by Benjamin Britten about a Suffolk fisherman.

clue.text: Change brought about in church promptly

indicators.note: brought about is a sailing term for turning round, so the hidden run is read backwards
in says the letters lie inside the words church promptly, across the word join

explanation.surface: Something altered in a congregation without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' looks like 'caused', but here it means turned round: churcH PROMptly holds HPROM, which read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To morph is to transform smoothly from one shape or form into another.

clue.text: Hard bargainer getting unusual rates in hotel booking

indicators.note: in tells us the jumbled letters go inside the hotel booking

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an order is a booking or reservation

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of rates are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tough negotiator securing odd room prices in a hotel reservation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns RATES into SETRA; 'in' puts that inside HORDER, after HOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse-trader is someone shrewd at hard bargaining, as horse dealers were reputed to be.

clue.text: Carry toddler with energy

parts.note: a tot is a small child, a toddler
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A parent lugging a lively little child.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is an informal word for to lug or haul something along.

clue.text: Island dweller, elder, hasn't changed

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the two words are rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: An old islander who has stayed set in their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges the ten letters of ELDER HASNT; 'hasn't changed' reads as stubbornness, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shetlander is a native or inhabitant of the Shetland Isles north of Scotland.

clue.text: Mischievous son about to disrupt gathering

indicators.note: disrupting a gathering means breaking into it, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a rally is a mass gathering or meeting
S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
CA is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A naughty boy about to break up a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to disrupt' puts S and CA inside RALLY, splitting it as RA...LLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rascally behaviour is roguish and full of tricks, like that of a scamp.

clue.text: Stepped inside a certain covered stadium

indicators.note: inside says the stepped word goes into the other letters

parts.note: some can mean a certain, as in some person
trod is the past tense of tread, stepped

explanation.surface: Walking into a particular indoor sports arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts TROD into A SOME, after AS. The Astrodome in Houston was the first domed sports stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: The Astrodome in Houston, Texas, was the world's first domed multipurpose sports arena.

clue.text: Question for children

definitions.meaning: a matter in dispute, a point to be decided
a legal word for a person's offspring

explanation.definitionFit: Issue means both a topic under debate and, formally, one's descendants or offspring.

clue.text: Mean man, mournful

parts.note: to mean to do something is to plan it
gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A miserly fellow looking sorrowful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' suggests stingy, but it is a verb meaning intend.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent sounds are loud and mournful, like a resounding lament.

clue.text: Outfit and hat without a spot on

parts.note: a rig, or rig-out, is an outfit of clothes

indicators.note: without here means lacking, so a letter goes out of the hat word

explanation.surface: Clothes and headgear without a single stain on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A from HAT, leaving HT after RIG. 'spot on' looks like a stain on the clothes, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is British slang for exactly correct, accurate.

clue.text: Brave soldier perhaps with impudence going ahead

indicators.note: going ahead says the impudence word comes before the soldier

parts.note: gall means cheek, impudence
a soldier ant is one kind of ant, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A fearless soldier pressing forward with cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier perhaps' points to an ant, since soldier ants are a caste of ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant means courageous and chivalrous, valiant.

clue.text: Lawyer finally after banality set about new, decisive argument

indicators.note: after says the lawyer's final letter comes behind the rest
set about means placed around, so the cliche goes round the new letter

parts.note: a cliche is a banal, overused phrase

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word lawyer

explanation.surface: A lawyer's closing point after a tired argument is reworked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' puts N inside CLICHE to give CLINCHE; 'finally' takes R from 'Lawyer', and 'after' sets it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A clincher is the point or fact that settles an argument conclusively.

clue.text: Making haste to catch start of extraordinary trial

indicators.note: to catch means to hold, so the haste word wraps round the first letter

parts.note: haring means rushing, running fast like a hare

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of the word extraordinary

explanation.surface: Rushing to see the opening of a sensational court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' takes E from 'extraordinary'; 'to catch' puts it inside HARING, after H.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearing is a trial or formal examination of a case before a court.

clue.text: Certainly upset to receive label 'excessively theatrical

indicators.note: to receive means to take in, so the turned word holds the label
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: yes means certainly, a firm agreement
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: Someone who gets upset at being labelled a drama queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns YES into SEY; 'to receive' puts TAG inside it, after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagey behaviour is overdone and artificial, as if acted on a stage.

clue.text: Dissatisfied number beginning to talk at back of large company being entertained by chap

indicators.note: at back of says the number and its added letter come behind the rest
a guest entertained by a host is taken in, so these letters go inside the chap word

parts.note: man is a synonym for chap
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
ten is a number

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the word talk

explanation.surface: An unhappy employee grumbling at the rear of a big firm's party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being entertained by' puts L and CO inside MAN; 'beginning to' takes T from 'talk'; 'at back of' sets TEN plus T after MALCON.
explanation.definitionFit: A malcontent is a discontented person; used as an adjective it means discontented, disaffected.

clue.text: Settled quietly, with relief

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
aid means relief, help given to those in need

explanation.surface: A bill quietly cleared, to everyone's relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A settled account is one that has been cleared by payment.

clue.text: Notice, during party, lower part of wall

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the notice goes inside the party

parts.note: a do is British slang for a party
an ad, advertisement, is a public notice

explanation.surface: A poster spotted at a party, low on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts AD inside DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado is the lower section of an interior wall, often panelled or edged with a rail.

clue.text: Hat has to be altered and returned in good condition

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters of has are rearranged
returned means sent back, so the two letters are read backwards

parts.note: OK means fine, in good condition

explanation.surface: Someone's hat sent off for repair and given back as good as new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be altered' turns HAS into SHA; 'returned' turns OK into KO.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall cylindrical military cap with a peak and plume.

clue.text: Soldier scrambled near ridge

indicators.note: scrambled tells us the letters of the two words are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier clambering up close to a mountain crest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' looks like the soldier's climb, but it signals rearranging the nine letters of NEAR RIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is a member of the Grenadier Guards or, originally, a soldier who threw grenades.

clue.text: Coldly determined and cunning, securing support

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the sly word wraps round the support

parts.note: sly means cunning, crafty
a tee is the peg that supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A ruthless schemer shoring up their backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' puts TEE inside SLY, splitting it as S...LY.
explanation.definitionFit: A steely manner is hard and unyielding, showing cold resolve like metal.

clue.text: Unwell after time in channel

indicators.note: after says the unwell word comes behind the time letter

parts.note: feeling rough is British slang for feeling unwell

explanation.surface: Someone feeling sick after some time crossing the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channel' suggests the English Channel and seasickness, but it is the definition, a groove or gutter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is a long narrow channel or gutter, for example for carrying water.
